sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Butts County, and who sets the value?
sections.html:
Two separate offices in Jackson handle the two halves of the job. The Butts County Board of Tax Assessors sets the value of your house, and the Butts County Tax Commissioner bills and collects the tax. Both sit in the building at 625 W. 3rd Street in Jackson, the assessors in Suite 1 and the tax commissioner in Suite 2.

The county's own tax pages say the tax commissioner is independent of the assessors and of the Board of Commissioners. That matters if you are selling: a question about a value goes to one counter, and a question about a balance, a payoff or a lien goes to the other.

  • Assessors: 770-775-8207, open to the public 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday through Friday.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-775-8206, open 8 AM to 4 PM, Monday through Friday except approved holidays.
  • Deeds and liens are recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, which is also where a copy of your warranty deed comes from.

The county and school boards each set their own millage rates. The Butts County assessor site explains that the tax is levied on an assessed value fixed by law at 40% of fair market value as of January 1, and that one mill equals $1.00 for each $1,000 of assessed value.

sections.h2: When are Butts County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate and personal property bills are split into two installments. The first is due September 15 and the second December 7, and if either date lands on a weekend it moves to the next business day. Mobile and manufactured homes are billed separately and are due April 1.

The tax commissioner's FAQ says bills go to the homeowner, never to the mortgage company. A data file does go to mortgage companies on record, but you are the one who has to forward a paper bill if your lender escrows the payment. After a sale, the new owner's bill follows the deed, so call the office if a bill arrives for a house you no longer own.

Partial payments are accepted, and you can make as many as you need. Interest and penalties keep running on whatever is left, and any account with a balance can be placed under a lien. Ask the tax commissioner whether a postmark counts for a mailed payment, because the FAQ page gives two different answers depending on the question.

sections.h2: What happened with the 2026 reappraisal in Butts County?
sections.html:
Butts County ran a countywide reappraisal for 2026. The Board of Commissioners hired Georgia Mass Appraisal Solutions, and its field staff began visiting parcels in July 2025. The assessors' notice says about 13,000 parcels were reviewed from the outside, with measurements and photos, and that appraisers do not go inside a home.

The project set values as of January 1, 2026, and the annual notices of assessment went out in April and May of 2026. On July 8, 2026 the Board of Assessors posted an official notice that more than 3% of total value was under appeal, which under Code Section 48-5-311(e)(3)(B) gave the board an extra 180 days to answer appeals for assessment year 2026.

For a seller, the practical point is that a 2026 value change may already be on your record. Pull the current value on the assessors' search page before you set a price, and ask whether any appeal on your parcel is still open. An unresolved appeal can change the number the tax commissioner bills.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Butts County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was sent. The appeal is in writing, filed with the Board of Assessors on form PT-311-A, and it must name the method you want. The tax commissioner's FAQ lists the grounds as taxability, value, uniformity or denial of an exemption.

The county's explainer on property tax says the assessors will look at your evidence first and can adjust the value if they find an error. If you still disagree, the next stop is the Board of Equalization, a panel of county residents appointed by the Grand Jury. An arbitration route exists as an alternative if you choose it when you file.

  • Bring proof of value: a recent appraisal, comparable sales, or photos of defects.
  • An appeal cannot be based on the size of the tax bill, only on the value or taxability behind it.
  • The assessors' forms page says the board cannot waive a deadline or relieve a penalty.

sections.h2: What exemptions and deadlines apply to a Butts County homeowner?
sections.html:
The standard homestead exemption is open to owners who live in the house, and the forms page lists an April 1 deadline. A separate form covers owners aged 62 or older, with a $20,000 county and $15,000 school exemption listed. You must own and occupy the home on January 1, and a move or a change in the deed means filing again.

Property tax returns for real and personal property run January 1 through April 1, and in Butts County they are filed at the assessors' office. Agricultural use valuation (form PT-283A) also carries an April 1 deadline, and the office asks you to call before filing.

If you buy or inherit a house, the exemption does not transfer automatically. A new owner who plans to live there needs to file their own application by the April 1 cutoff for that year.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes go unpaid on a Butts County house?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner mails a 30-day notice of intent before a lien, called a FiFa, is issued. Unpaid tax can be recorded as a FiFa on the General Execution Docket kept by the Clerk of Superior Court once it is more than 90 days past due, according to the county's FAQ. Paying the tax along with the fees, interest and penalties cancels the lien.

The office does not sell liens over the counter. If legal action such as a levy and advertisement for a tax sale has begun, the FAQ advises paying in person. A recorded lien is a public record that can show up on your credit file, and the tax office says it has no control over how credit bureaus use it.

A lien will block a clean title, so a title company will want it paid at or before closing. Ask the tax commissioner for a written payoff figure with a good-through date, and give that figure to whoever is handling the closing.

sections.h2: What is Butts County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Butts County is a West Central Georgia county of about 184 square miles, created in December 1825 from parts of Henry and Monroe counties. Jackson is the county seat and largest city, with Flovilla and Jenkinsburg as the other two incorporated cities. Interstate 75 runs through it, along with U.S. 23 and State Routes 16, 36, 42 and 87.

The county sits in the Atlanta metro area, borders Henry, Spalding, Lamar, Monroe, Jasper and Newton counties, and is known for Jackson Lake, formed by the 1910 Lloyd Shoals dam on the Ocmulgee River, and for Indian Springs State Park.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Butts County house if the property tax is behind?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent tax is paid out of the sale at closing, so the lien is cleared as part of the transaction. Ask the Butts County Tax Commissioner at 770-775-8206 for a payoff amount with a good-through date, since interest and penalties grow each month.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a bill versus a value?
faqs.a: Call the tax commissioner at 770-775-8206 about a bill, a payoff or a lien, and the Board of Assessors at 770-775-8207 about value, exemptions or an appeal. The two offices share a building on W. 3rd Street in Jackson but answer to different authorities.

faqs.q: Does my mortgage company get my Butts County tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The bill is mailed to the owner, and the county only sends a data file to mortgage companies on record. If your lender pays from escrow, forward the bill yourself, and check with the lender if it has recently changed.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to file a homestead exemption in Butts County?
faqs.a: April 1. The assessors' forms page lists April 1 for the standard homestead exemption and for the age 62 and over exemption. An application filed after that date applies to the next tax year.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Butts County assessment?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date the assessment notice was sent. File in writing with the Board of Assessors, and keep your proof of value ready. The board has no power to extend that window.
